note: Saturday 07:00 SGT re-verify (weekend, pre-Asia-open) against the Fri 24 Jul US close. The mid-week oil shock partially UNWOUND on Friday — WTI fell -4.7% to ~$87.88 and Brent slipped to ~$98.38 (back under $100) — but the damage rotated: Treasury yields pushed to year-highs (10Y ~4.71%, 2Y ~4.37%) and a firm dollar (DXY ~101.5) crushed the metals complex, silver -3.5% to ~$57.64 (breaking below the $58 line) and gold -2% to ~$4,048. Equities held (S&P ~7,408, roughly flat on the day but a soft week for Dow/Nasdaq) with VIX contained ~18.6 and credit very tight (HY OAS ~268bp). Sentiment sits in FEAR (CNN ~41, crypto 28). Fear&Greed is fetched LIVE in-browser with the baked value as fallback; breadth & regional flows are researched (no free real-time API). CNN's page geoblocked (HTTP 451) again this run, so the 7 sub-components are INFERRED from the ~41 composite and cited internals (VIX ~18.6, HY ~268bp, ~69% >200-DMA) and labeled as such.

That broad-but-tiring backdrop meets low-40s Fear sentiment and a metals/rate stress that hit Materials hardest. Several sub-metrics (50-DMA %, daily A/D, net new highs, exact McClellan value) are approximate or lagged as labeled. The open question into the 28-29 Jul FOMC: whether a hawkish hold deepens the metals/rate stress or a data-dependent Warsh eases the pressure.

flows.period: BofA 'Flow Show'/EPFR week ended 8 Jul 2026 (freshest verifiable weekly), plus the prior week to 1 Jul and the July BofA Global Fund Manager Survey. Weekly flows lag ~2-6 days and PRE-DATE the late-July metals/yield stress — read the positioning theme, not any single number. Labeled EARLY-JULY 2026.
flows.narrative: The freshest verifiable weekly read (to ~8 Jul) was strongly risk-on: global equity funds drew +$56.6bn (the 4th-largest weekly inflow of the year) with Tech funds alone +$18.8bn, even as money-market assets swelled +$39.5bn to a record ~$7.9tn — cash is being deployed into equities AND still building. That followed a sharp -$17.2bn US-equity outflow the prior week (to ~1 Jul) that rotated into IG bonds (+$17.2bn) and Japan. The bigger tell is positioning: BofA's July Global FMS shows cash at just 3.6% of AUM ('uber-low', lowest since Feb) — tripping the contrarian Cash-Rule SELL signal — with a net +42% overweight equities and the Bull & Bear Indicator at 9.5 (also a sell signal). So flows and surveys both read stretched-bullish into the late-July rate/metals stress. Per-region weekly detail (EM/China/Europe/gold) beyond the 'rotation to Japan/bonds' note was not itemized in retrievable free sources this run.
